raw.assessment: The incumbent achieved the intended course set in 32/40 exports (80%) and a 17-minute median, below the stated targets. Its seven-minute median for unchanged assignments suggests a useful baseline, without establishing causation. Six affected exports coincided with assignment changes; the two renamed-course cases limit an assignment-only explanation. Fast execution and slow replacement delivery suggest a separate coordination delay, but handling components were not measured. Zero observed cross-center rows does not establish isolation for the unsampled split-course center.

openings.claim: Using current instructor assignments for a requested week may omit or misselect courses after an assignment change; selection using the relevant assignment intervals could prevent some affected exports.
openings.delta: Make the requested week relevant to course selection rather than relying solely on present assignments.
openings.prediction: With identical attendance and course identities, changing only the current assignment will change incumbent selection if this mechanism operates; interval-aware selection will retain the agreed weekly course set.
openings.probe: In staging, compare unchanged and midweek reassignment fixtures against coordinator-agreed weekly course sets. Inspect selection before CSV generation, verify the documented CSV schema and tenant isolation, and attempt concurrent attendance entry. Estimate implementation effort and hosting cost before adopting a fix.
assumptions: Assignment history is available or recoverable without guessing.
Coordinators can specify inclusion for a course reassigned within a week.
A production change fits six engineer-days and existing hosting; this is unverified.

openings.claim: Were renamed courses actually absent, or did their exported names fail to match coordinators' timetables?
openings.delta: Distinguish data omission from recognition failure before treating both as export-selection defects.
openings.prediction: Recognition failure leaves the intended course rows present while a name mapping resolves the perceived absence; actual omission leaves expected rows missing even after names are reconciled.
openings.probe: Use a short coordinator session with fabricated renamed-course fixtures, the documented CSV, and old/new timetable labels. Compare expected and exported course identities internally, observe checking and importing, and time these steps separately.
assumptions: Internal course identity can be traced without changing the import schema.
Fabricated tasks provide useful diagnostic evidence but cannot establish production success rates.

raw.assessment: Assignment changes and renames coincide with affected exports, but the observations do not establish the selection failure's cause. One counterfactual opening is warranted; its handling-time and implementation feasibility remain unproved.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: forbid current instructor assignment as an export-selection dependency. Within the private service, let an authorized coordinator approve a center-and-week manifest of course identifiers, including courses with zero attendance. The exporter selects only that manifest's courses and the requested week's attendance, independently enforcing center ownership on every participant row, and emits the existing CSV schema.
openings.delta: Moves the intended course set into an explicit, reusable weekly decision instead of deriving it from present instructor assignments. Renames retain identifiers; splits require an explicit decision about which resulting courses belong to the requested week. This could reduce repeated reconciliation, but initial approval may add work.
openings.prediction: Holding attendance and the approved manifest fixed, changing only a current instructor assignment will leave the exported course set unchanged. Incorrect or stale manifests will still produce incorrect course sets. Improved selection will reduce total handling only if manifest preparation costs less than the checking and correction it replaces.
openings.probe: In fabricated staging, compare existing selection with manifest selection across assignment changes, renames, zero-attendance courses, and splits. Attempt foreign-center course and participant references; require no foreign records. During exports, verify attendance entry remains available. Use the six coordinators' two short sessions to establish intended sets independently, then time preparation, checking, correction, download, and import. Reject implementation if the dependency audit exceeds six engineer-days or hosting allowance. If feasible, evaluate the next 40 exports against all three success thresholds.
assumptions: Replacement dependencies: persistent center-scoped course identifiers and attendance-to-course links; a private manifest store/editor; explicit requested-week boundaries and split/rename mapping; authorized coordinators with sufficiently complete timetable evidence and time to approve manifests; independent center authorization and row ownership checks; the existing CSV renderer and authorized workspace delivery; nonblocking, consistent reads while attendance continues; implementation within six engineer-days and existing hosting capacity.
These capabilities and costs require verification. Privacy, CSV compatibility, budget, and uninterrupted attendance entry remain mandatory; none is relaxed.

openings.claim: Relevant assignment intervals may restore weekly selection.
openings.discriminator: Changing current assignments alters incumbent selection but not interval-aware selection.
openings.probe: Hold attendance/identities fixed; compare unchanged/reassigned staging fixtures against agreed weekly sets before CSV generation.
openings.uncertainty: History, midweek inclusion rules and feasibility unverified; correlation is not causation.

openings.claim: Renames may cause recognition failure or omission.
openings.discriminator: Reconciled identities distinguish present-but-unrecognized from missing rows.
openings.probe: Observe fabricated rename checking/importing with old/new labels; trace identities internally and time steps.
openings.uncertainty: Schema-preserving identity tracing unverified; fabricated results cannot establish production success.

openings.claim: Authorized center/week course-ID manifests replace assignment-based selection, include zero-attendance courses, preserve rename identities and explicitly decide splits.
openings.discriminator: Fixed attendance/manifests withstand assignment changes; stale manifests still fail.
openings.probe: Compare reassignment/rename/zero-attendance/split fixtures; test foreign course/participant references. Six coordinators, two sessions: independently establish intended sets; time preparation/checking/correction/download/import.
openings.uncertainty: Needs scoped IDs/links, private editor/store, week/split mappings, timely complete timetables, authorization/row ownership, authorized delivery and consistent nonblocking reads. Approval overhead may erase savings.

post_distill.decision: Diagnose before choosing D1/D3. Verify private/authorized processing, existing CSV, <=6 engineer-days, existing hosting, concurrent attendance and isolation including splits. Zero sampled leaks excludes the split center. Replacement-delivery delay remains separate; handling components unmeasured. If feasible, assess next 40: median <=12 minutes, intended sets >=95%, zero foreign records. Evidence: stipulated synthetic.
